items.action: Where your theme or brand sets `--ds-link-color` on `:root` as its link colour, set `--text-link` there instead, in each theme block it applies to. Where you read `var(--ds-link-color)`, or a palette value standing for the link colour (`var(--blue-700)`, `hsl(var(--blue-h) 90% 74%)`), outside `.link`, read `var(--text-link)`.
items.appliesWhen: `--text-link` is a theme role in both themes: `var(--blue-700)` in light, `hsl(var(--blue-h) 90% 74%)` in dark, blue under any brand. `.link` reads `var(--ds-link-color, var(--text-link))` from `styles/link`, which `styles/ds` forwards, and a `ds-table` cell link reads the same role. `--ds-link-color` is the `.link` hook, set on `.link` or an ancestor; a theme that sets it on `:root` recolours `.link` and not the table cell link.
items.pitfall: The dark theme declares `--text-link` under `:root[data-theme='dark']`, which outranks a plain `:root` rule, so a brand that sets it only on `:root` keeps the blue dark link; restate it under `[data-theme='dark']` as for `--primary`.
items.verify: No stylesheet sets `--ds-link-color` on `:root` as a theme role or reads a `--blue-*` value as the link colour, and in light and dark a `.link` and a `ds-table` cell link paint in the colour the brand intends.

items.action: Where your theme or brand sets `--ds-link-color-visited` on `:root` as its visited link colour, set `--text-link-visited` there instead, in each theme block it applies to. Where you read `var(--ds-link-color-visited)` or a palette value standing for the visited link colour outside `.link`, read `var(--text-link-visited)`. To keep visited links in the link colour, set `--text-link-visited: var(--text-link)` in both theme blocks.
items.appliesWhen: `--text-link-visited` is a theme role in both themes: `hsl(var(--blue-h) calc(var(--blue-s) * 0.6) 45%)` in light, `hsl(var(--blue-h) 50% 70%)` in dark. A visited `.link` reads `var(--ds-link-color-visited, var(--text-link-visited))` from `styles/link`, which `styles/ds` forwards. `.link.quiet`, a link with `aria-disabled="true"` and a `<button class="link">` keep their colour.
items.pitfall: Browsers ignore custom properties declared inside a `:visited` rule, so `.link:visited { --text-link-visited: red; }` does nothing; set the role in the theme block or `--ds-link-color-visited` on `.link` or an ancestor.
items.verify: No stylesheet sets `--ds-link-color-visited` on `:root` as a theme role or reads a `--blue-*` value as the visited link colour, and a visited `.link` paints in the colour the app intends in light and dark.

items.appliesWhen: A stylesheet written against 0.15.0 that sets `--link-visited` in a theme block or reads `var(--link-visited)`. `--text-link`, `--ds-link-color` and `--ds-link-color-visited` keep their names. The default moved with the name: 0.15.0 built `--link-visited`, and the dark `--text-link`, from `--primary-h` and `--primary-s`; `--text-link-visited` and the dark `--text-link` take `--blue-h` and `--blue-s`, so under a brand that sets `--primary-h` or `--primary-s` both stay blue.
items.pitfall: The old name is inert rather than invalid: a declaration left behind sets nothing, and a read left behind resolves to nothing, so the element takes its inherited colour with no error. A brand that relied on 0.15.0 deriving the visited or dark link colour from `--primary-h` must set `--text-link-visited`, and the dark `--text-link`, itself.
items.verify: No stylesheet declares or reads `--link-visited`, and a visited `.link` paints in the colour the app intends in light and dark.

items.action: None, unless a `ds-table` cell link must stay in the brand colour: set `--ds-table-cell-link-color: var(--accent)` on `ds-table` or an ancestor.
items.appliesWhen: A `ds-table` column with `link`, and an `interactive: true` cell of a `rowInteractive` table on row hover. `--ds-table-cell-link-color` defaults to `var(--text-link)` where it was `var(--accent)`: `--blue-700` where it was `--blue-600` in light, the light dark-theme link blue where it was the dark `--primary`, and blue under a brand that set `--primary`. A table that sets `--ds-table-cell-link-color` itself keeps its colour.
items.pitfall: A brand that set `--primary` to colour its table links gets blue table links with no error; set `--text-link` for every link, or `--ds-table-cell-link-color` for the table alone.
items.verify: In light and dark, a `ds-table` link cell and a hovered `interactive` cell paint in `--text-link`, or in the colour the app sets, at 4.5:1 or more on the row.

informational.text: `showChange` on `dsLineSeries` and `ds-line-chart` colours the stretch from a reading of 0 in `--ds-chart-positive-color` or `--ds-chart-negative-color` like any other stretch, and prints no percentage on it.
informational.verify: Hover the reading after a 0 on a ds-line-chart with showChange and confirm the stretch from the 0 is thickened in the rising or falling colour with no percentage above it.

informational.text: The `showChange` stretch and percentage wait `--ds-motion-chart-mark-exit-duration` and fade in over `--ds-motion-chart-mark-enter-duration` (120ms and 400ms by default), as the chart's other marks do, such as a heatmap cell or a pie slice, and leave on `--ds-motion-chart-mark-exit-duration` and `--ds-motion-chart-mark-exit-easing`.
informational.verify: Hover a reading on a ds-line-chart with showChange and confirm the percentage appears after a short pause and fades in over about 400ms.

informational.text: A `ds-table` under a `display: none` ancestor, such as an inactive `ds-tabs` panel, no longer measures its header labels or its `width: 'content'` columns there; it measures them when it is shown, so a `width: 'content'` column no longer collapses to 0px and no column shrinks below its header label after the table is shown.
informational.verify: Render a ds-table with a width: 'content' column inside an inactive ds-tabs panel, change its data there, switch to the panel, and confirm the column fits its widest cell and every column is at least as wide as its header label.
